artifact.rationale:
Translations are built from inputs.destination_profile and the repo snapshot. Evidence is incomplete: inventory analysis is 'unconfigured', controls_describe returned gate_unreachable, and the source IAM role and S3 bucket policy documents are not in /src (eks-values.yaml only has EXAMPLE placeholders and names the Pod Identity association chat/chat-app). Source ids are therefore logical names (terraform outputs attachments_bucket and db_secret_arn, Pod Identity chat/chat-app), not verified ARNs, so risk is high.
(1) The RGW bucket policy targets bucket bravo-demo-attachments. It allows only the OBC app principal s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject, denies non-TLS traffic (aws:SecureTransport=false), and denies every principal other than the app (NotPrincipal deny on Get, Put, Delete and List). This covers the OBJ-01 (anonymous) and OBJ-05 (other credentials) regressions in gate:a2083983-d811-4430-a37d-4d951e520d6b:obj-01 and gate:a2083983-d811-4430-a37d-4d951e520d6b:obj-05. Anonymous list is not allowed by any statement. NOTE: the app is granted no s3:ListBucket; if the app needs it, a later attempt must add it.
(2) Secrets Manager (inv:3ccbf876f57f08e8, inv:9de663601b600ca9, inv:c6b9dab5de3d8a70) becomes an OpenBao policy app-target-onprem-chat-bravo-demo. It has read only on secret/data/envs/target-onprem/chat-db (kv v2, inside path_prefix) and no list. An ExternalSecret chat-bravo-demo-db via ClusterSecretStore bravo-platform-openbao fills Secret bravo-demo-db key password from property app_writer, mounted as DB_PASSWORD_FILE.
(3) IAM to RBAC: a namespaced Role and RoleBinding in chat for SA chat-bravo-demo with get on resourceNames [bravo-demo-db] only. No list or watch, no cluster scope.
Target names avoid the reserved 'bravo-' prefix, which policy_evaluate flagged. The S3 endpoint swap (inv:baa6de5a5e72c850, inv:4b2a570efa066af8) and the GCS literal (inv:ecedbaf5b23990db) belong to other roles. Postgres DSN needs no change (inv:a5ccbeca75df0ace).

exception_justifications.justification: The source policies don't encode at-rest encryption (SSE or KMS). On-prem, encryption at rest belongs to the RGW and OpenBao storage backends, not to bucket or access policy. No translation is proposed. Platform evidence is needed for a human to review.

Audit logging (the CloudTrail equivalent) comes from RGW ops logs and the OpenBao audit device, which are set outside these policies. No source audit config was found in the snapshot. Platform confirmation is required.
Backup and replication of the bucket and the KV mount are not expressed in IAM, bucket or secret policies, and the snapshot has no source DR configuration. Left for platform review.

artifact.audit_summary:
For the human approver: four destination artifacts are proposed. None of this is a verdict; no control is marked as passed.
1) rgw_bucket_policy chat-bravo-demo-attachments (bucket bravo-demo-attachments). App OBC user gets Get and Put on objects. Plaintext HTTP is denied for all. Everyone other than the app is denied Get, Put, Delete and List. Addresses OBJ-01 and OBJ-05 destination regressions. Controls: IAM-01, NET-01, ENC-02 (in-transit TLS enforcement), ISO-01.
2) openbao_policy app-target-onprem-chat-bravo-demo: read on secret/data/envs/target-onprem/chat-db only. Controls: SEC-01, IAM-01.
3) external_secret chat-bravo-demo-db in ns chat: syncs app_writer into Secret bravo-demo-db/password via ClusterSecretStore bravo-platform-openbao. This replaces the direct Secrets Manager SDK call. Controls: SEC-01, ISO-01.
4) k8s_rbac chat-bravo-demo: namespaced Role with get on Secret bravo-demo-db, bound to SA chat-bravo-demo. Controls: IAM-01, ISO-01.
Not covered: ENC-01 (at-rest encryption on RGW and OpenBao is a platform setting), AUD-01 (RGW ops log and OpenBao audit device) and DR-01. There is no source evidence to translate for these. Please confirm them on the platform side.
Caveats: the gate was unreachable, the source IAM and bucket policy JSON was not available, and source ids are logical names. Confirm whether the app needs s3:ListBucket or DeleteObject. Confirm that RGW honours NotPrincipal and aws:SecureTransport in the test-bucket Job.

artifact.rationale: Removed the direct Secrets Manager SDK client and call (inv:3ccbf876f57f08e8 at secrets.py:41, inv:9de663601b600ca9 at secrets.py:48), the boto3/botocore imports and the json import that was no longer used. db_password() now reads only the mounted file named by DB_PASSWORD_FILE. In the landing zone, ESO syncs this file from OpenBao into the bravo-demo-db Secret, mounted at /var/run/bravo/db/password. In config.py I removed the DB_PASSWORD_SOURCE selector and the DB_PASSWORD_SECRET_ID/_KEY/_REGION/_ENDPOINT_URL keys (the region could also come from AWS_REGION), and dropped the matching DbSettings fields. DB_PASSWORD_FILE is now required and is the only password input, so the app starts with just DB_DSN and DB_PASSWORD_FILE, as the destination provides. password_source is kept as the constant "env-file" so the startup logs in app.py and secrets.py keep their content without touching app.py. Nothing else changed: DSN handling and the check that rejects a password in the DSN, the S3/attachments config (inv:baa6de5a5e72c850 and inv:4b2a570efa066af8 already read S3_ENDPOINT_URL from env, so there is no per-cloud path), the write-block switch and logging. No dependencies, tests, CI or deploy files were touched, and no credentials were added. compile passed, and the diff is the make_diff output exactly. Note: the tool view showed the DSN password-check line in config.py partly as [redacted]. I rebuilt it from the visible pieces, and make_diff shows no change on that line (it is identical to /src). I then kept that line's error message unchanged so the line does not appear in the diff at all. One small leftover: that unchanged message still says "use DB_PASSWORD_SOURCE". Risk is medium, not low, because I could not search the tests (the search check would not run). Tests that build DbSettings with the removed secret_* fields, or that exercise the aws-secrets-manager mode, would now fail. That failure would be intended, but I have not checked it. The gate regressions OBJ-01 and OBJ-05 (gate:a2083983-d811-4430-a37d-4d951e520d6b:obj-01, :obj-05) are presumably the DB-password startup failure on the destination, but the evidence summaries do not say so.
